rules.body: Apply when introducing delayed persistence into an editor whose document work outlives its view subscription and whose saves may synchronously navigate. README.md: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate." docs/host-api.md: "Document buffers are owned by the coordinator dictionary, while Badge owns only a live subscription."

Route active-document edits through the existing document-keyed trailing task. Each edit replaces the pending text and restarts the 120 ms interval; consumption writes the latest text to that document's captured identity. Keep the task reusable across bursts. TASK: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." src/services.js: "push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); },"

Keep document-buffer ownership in the coordinator dictionary independently of subscription cleanup. Reconcile pending persistent edits when opening another document, closing, or disposing; ending the badge subscription must not discard those edits. Flushing the departing buffer is one suitable strategy. README.md: "Document-buffer responsibility: coordinator dictionary". TASK: "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." src/coordinator.js establishes the prior persistence behavior: "edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}"

Preserve the trailing utility's clear-before-consume ordering so synchronous callbacks cannot flush the same pending value again or erase newly queued work during later cleanup. src/services.js: "const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };"

Treat a departure save as a synchronous reentry boundary. Detach the departing view and perform its subscription and render cleanup before flushing; after flushing, validate the outer navigation's authority before publishing its requested view. Do not perform stale outer cleanup or publication over navigation initiated by a save callback. docs/host-api.md: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." README.md: "Save callbacks can synchronously navigate."

Preserve public operations, document identities, exact text including empty text, and status payload semantics. Keep the current view's live status subscription behavior. docs/host-api.md: "createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide()." and "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics."

Leave search-preview behavior outside the change; do not transfer persistent-document departure policy to its transient task. TASK: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/services.js: "const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));" and "return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};"

Use explicitly controlled timers to check no intermediate burst writes, exactly the latest text after 120 ms of quiet, subsequent-burst reuse, and valid empty text. Check persistence across switch, close, dispose, and reopen; during departure saves, synchronously invoke open or close and verify the newer navigation remains authoritative without stale renders. Check status payload preservation and unchanged preview delay, hide cancellation, and reuse. These checks operationalize TASK's "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." and docs/host-api.md's "Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled."

limitations: Departure flushing is a source-supported preservation strategy, not an explicitly prescribed algorithm in TASK.
The guidance applies to persistent document work with separate view subscriptions and synchronous save callbacks; transient work may require cancellation instead.
Exception recovery, use after disposal, and inputs outside the documented text interface are unspecified.

Attempt 1 reports passing observations, but one successful implementation does not establish causality, exhaustive correctness, or benefit across tasks. AST hints and evaluation observations do not add requirements.

notes: Not approved; training acceptance or expert summary does not verify cross-task effectiveness
